summary: Records the text of the Memorandum of Understanding between the IETF and ICANN about the technical work of the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority, signed on March 1, 2000 and ratified by the ICANN Board on March 10, 2000. It is an informational memo.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 2860 records an agreement between the IETF and ICANN about IANA's technical work for IETF and IRTF protocols. It says assignments follow RFC rules and explains who gives technical guidance when questions arise. The agreement does not cover broader domain-name or address-allocation policy.

subtitle: The IETF-ICANN agreement recorded for IANA's technical parameter work.

tldr.problem: The IETF and ICANN needed to record how IANA would handle technical assignments for protocols within the IETF's scope.
tldr.mechanism: The Memorandum of Understanding directs IANA to follow RFC criteria and procedures, seek technical guidance from the IESG, and refer technical disputes between IANA and the IESG to the IAB.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2860 records the MoU signed in 2000. It excludes broader policy issues about domain names and IP address blocks from its scope.

today: RFC 2860 is Informational, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It records the text of the IETF-ICANN MoU signed in March 2000.

sections.title: What the Memorandum Records
sections.content:
RFC 2860 places on record a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the IETF and ICANN concerning the technical work of the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA). The MoU was signed on March 1, 2000, and ratified by the ICANN Board on March 10, 2000.

The agreement covers IANA's technical work on behalf of the IETF and the Internet Research Task Force (IRTF). It remains in effect until changed by mutual consent or cancelled with at least six months' notice.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC records an agreement about IANA's technical work for Internet protocol registries. It also states how the agreement can be changed or ended.

sections.title: The Organizations and Roles
sections.content:
The MoU identifies IANA as the technical team that makes and publishes protocol-parameter assignments; the document says that team is part of ICANN. The IETF creates Internet Standards and related documents, while the IAB is its oversight committee and designates IANA on the IETF's behalf.

The Internet Engineering Steering Group (IESG) manages the IETF. For IRTF-related parameters, the agreement substitutes the IRTF and Internet Research Steering Group for the IETF and IESG procedures, with the IAB resolving questions about which organization applies.
sections.plainLanguage: The agreement defines the groups involved before describing their responsibilities. It also explains which process applies when an assignment concerns IRTF work.

sections.title: How Technical Assignments Are Decided
sections.content:
IANA assigns and registers protocol parameters according to the criteria and procedures specified in RFCs. If an RFC is unclear or silent, IANA follows past and current practice unless the IESG directs otherwise.

For technical questions or disputes, IANA seeks guidance from the IESG, which may appoint an expert. If IANA and the IESG disagree technically, they seek IAB guidance, and the MoU says the IAB's decision is final. Policy issues about domain names and IP address blocks are outside the agreement, with specified technical-use exceptions remaining in scope.
sections.plainLanguage: IANA follows the assignment rules written in RFCs. The IESG gives technical guidance, and the IAB resolves technical disputes between the IANA and IESG.

sections.title: Public Records, Requests, and Appeals
sections.content:
IANA must make information about current assignments, including contact details for assignees, available online without charge. It must provide online facilities for assignment requests and may deny requests only for legitimate technical reasons.

For IETF-scope protocols, applicants can appeal a denial to the IESG and then to the IAB. IANA also has non-voting liaison seats on appropriate IETF committees and reviews documents during IETF Last Call to raise concerns with the IESG.
sections.plainLanguage: The agreement calls for public assignment records and online request facilities. It also gives applicants a path to appeal a technical denial.

sections.title: Effect and Limits of the Agreement
sections.content:
The MoU says it does not make the parties business partners or agents of one another, and neither party may transfer its rights or duties without written consent. The agreement required ICANN Board approval or ratification.

The RFC says the document does not directly affect Internet security. It also records that domain-name and IP-address policy questions are beyond its technical scope.
sections.plainLanguage: The MoU defines technical responsibilities without making the organizations business partners. It does not settle broader policy decisions about names or address blocks.
